CORRECTION AND FULL MAP. My earlier handoff said "58 call sites". That number was wrong — a grep that swept up ManagedController.submit, SlurmCommands.submit, submitAt and friends. The real surface, measured properly:

- 1 trait declaration: core/Scheduler.scala:12
- 21 implementations of submit: 6 main (SlurmCliScheduler:24, SlurmLocal:51 export, TelemetryScheduler:79, RemoteSlurm:50, SchedulerStub:20, ScriptedScheduler:20) and 15 in tests, of which most are one-line `unused`/`unexpected` stubs
- 22 call sites: 7 main (ManagedController:302, AgentService:186, RegisteredTaskService:26/:51/:94, RegisteredTaskLauncher:1356/:1372) and 15 in tests
- 1 lowering to delete: ssh/Slurm.scala:282-304
- 1 wire codec pair: AgentDomainJson.scala:23/:46

So it is roughly half what I estimated, and most of it is mechanical.

TWO FINDINGS THAT CHANGE THE PLAN:

1. The wire is ALREADY LaunchSpec-shaped. encodeSubmitRequest emits a flat submissionKey, name, source, arguments, resources, environment, resultContract, array, retrySafety — the payload is already destructured into source/arguments and resultContract is a hardcoded "exit-only" string. The designed LaunchSpec is a near-exact match; the only wire delta is replacing that hardcoded string with a real descriptor.

2. THE BLOCKER, and it is not a code problem. managed/ManagedModel.scala:78-96 enforces a canonicalization round-trip law: decode, re-encode, require byte-identical output. And :168 derives attemptId FROM THE CANONICAL DIGEST. So changing the encoded field set invalidates every existing journal AND every stored attemptId — this is a durable-state format change, not just a wire change.

That is an argument for doing it NOW rather than later (nothing is published, no journals exist in the wild, and P7.6 has not cut a baseline), but it is the owner's call because it decides whether any existing local journal survives. It should be made explicitly, not as a side effect of a refactor.

CONFIRMED: A is purely phantom past the submit boundary. DurableResultHandle (core/StructuredResult.scala:29-41) has NO type parameter; typed recovery is runtime ResultSchemaId equality (ssh/RemoteTask.scala:336, managed/ResultAttachment.scala:58). RegisteredTaskLauncher:115 recovers A only via an @unchecked cast. Erasing the parameter loses no capability.

ALSO ERASABLE, and worth doing in the same pass since they exist only to feed submit and each reads only untyped fields: SubmissionPlanner.prepare[A] / PreparedSubmission[A] (cli/CliModel.scala:38-47), SiteProfile.resolve[A] (core/SiteProfile.scala:175, reads resources and array), ManagedRequestPolicy.validate[A] (managed/ManagedRequestPolicy.scala:6, reads environment).

WHERE LaunchSpec SHOULD BE PRODUCED: RegisteredTaskLauncher.scala:419-425 already performs the correct lowering, preserving the result contract — unlike ssh erase, which replaces it with ExitOnly. That is the model to generalize.
